html:
Venezuela's oil age began in earnest on 14 December 1922, when the Barroso II well at Cabimas on Lake Maracaibo blew out, spraying oil for nine days. By 1929 Venezuela was the world's largest oil exporter.

Foreign companies such as Shell and Standard Oil rushed in under the generous terms of Juan Vicente Gómez. Oil towns rose on the lake, and farming, once based on cacao and coffee, declined as people moved to the cities. In the 1940s new laws gave the state half the profits, and in 1960 Venezuela led the founding of OPEC. The oil industry was nationalised in 1976.

Oil paid for roads, universities and a large middle class, but made the country depend on one product, as Pérez Alfonzo warned. Falling prices and mismanagement later led to the collapse of Venezuela's economy.
sum: Venezuela's oil age began in earnest on 14 December 1922, when the Barroso II well at Cabimas on Lake Maracaibo blew out, spraying oil for nine days. By 1929 Venezuela was the world's largest oil exporter.
